titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 7/2010 (ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ އިދާރީ ދާއިރާތައް ލާމަރުކަޒީ އުސޫލުން ހިންގުމުގެ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ... ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This government bill amends the Decentralization Act (Law 7/2010) to change how empty seats on local councils are filled. Today the law says a by-election must be held within 60 days of the Elections Commission being told of a vacancy; the bill extends this to within 183 days. A by-election would not be required if 365 days or less remain in the council's term. The 60-day limit stays only when a council has too few members left to hold a legal meeting. The bill also sets deadlines for councils to pick a new vice president or deputy mayor when that post becomes vacant.
whyItMatters: Council seats could stay empty for up to about six months instead of two, and fewer separate by-elections would be held, which the government says would cut election costs.
keyProvisions: Articles 15, 29 and 45 are rewritten as rules on holding a by-election when a council president's or council member's post becomes vacant during the council's term.

The Local Government Authority must tell the Elections Commission within 14 days of a post becoming vacant, and a member must be elected to the empty seat within 183 days of that notice (replacing the current 60 days).
If 365 days or less remain in the council's term when the post becomes vacant, electing a replacement is not required (the current law uses one year).

If vacancies leave a council without enough members for the legal quorum to meet, members must be elected within 60 days of the last vacancy being reported; anyone elected in a by-election serves only until the council's term ends.

Articles 16, 26 and 42 are changed so that a vacant vice president post (atoll and island councils) or deputy mayor post (city councils) is filled by electing a member within 30 days, or within 7 days if the president or mayor post is also vacant.
The changes take effect once the law is passed, ratified and published in the government gazette (clause 7).
whoIsAffected: Atoll, island and city councils and their members, residents of areas with empty council seats, the Local Government Authority and the Elections Commission.
statedReasons: The note says vacancies on councils keep rising, forcing repeated by-elections within 60 days and higher costs, so the government wants to allow up to 183 days to hold them, keeping 60 days only when a council lacks enough members for a quorum.
